newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Motorola active on stock drop.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Motorola active on stock drop.

text.p: Motorola Inc puts and calls were active in early trading on the American Stock Exchange as the shares fell sharply but then recovered slightly after the company warned about its third quarter profits.
Early Wednesday, Motorola said it expected a "significant" drop in third quarter earnings per share, which it said could mean a decline of 25 percent or moree.
The company blamed the turndown mainly on its semiconductor business.
Motorola shares were down 1-3/4 at 48-7/8 by 1005 CDT (1505 GMT) on consolidated volume of roughly 5.85 million shares.
The stock had reached an early low of 46-3/4 before recovering.
The most active Motorola option in early trading was the October 50 put, with more than 3,900 contracts traded. The option gained 9/16 to 2-5/8.
The October 50 call traded 2,446 contracts and was down 1-3/16 at 1-13/15. The September 50 put traded 2,700 contracts.
Marty Kearney at PTI Securities said volatility on the Motorola puts had understandably risen moderately as the stock declined. He said volatility on the calls had remained steady.
Volatilities have trended higher over the past month, added Joseph Sunderman, a research analyst at Investment Research Institute in Cincinnati.

In conjunction with the pickup in volatilities, put volume had risen by about 15 percent compared with a rise of nearly four percent in call volume, suggesting investors were positioning themselves for a decline in the stock.

On Wednesday, put volume overall outpaced call volume by about three to one in morning action, but Hank Nothnagel, senior vice president of options trading at Everen Securities, said he saw call buyers emerging.
"We've got quite a few call buyers who are looking at this as a temporary downturn and then it's going to be business as usual," he said.
Sunderman said investors had been adding puts over the last week in expectation that the stock would break below the key 50 strike.
"They've been adding puts at the 50 strike all week long on the September and October series," he said. "They were adding calls, but were adding puts at a heavier pace."
He said the action was surprising because most times the bulk of investors place the wrong bets.
From a chart perspective, the 50-51 area for Motorola could be key because that zone has proved to be support several times since early this year, Sunderman added.
"This area has been huge for this stock and it's going to be interesting how it plays out over the next few hours and days to see if it recovers or breaks" down further, he said.
